newsitem.title: USA: Manufactured Home not considering increasing bid.
newsitem.headline: Manufactured Home not considering increasing bid.

text.p: Manufactured Home Communities Inc said Wednesday it is not considering increasing its bid for fellow mobile home park operate Chateau Properties Inc.
"We are not considering sweetening the offer," said David Helfand, chief executive of Manufactured Home Communities.

Earlier Wednesday, Clinton Township, Michigan-based Chateau said it rejected a revised merger offer from Manufactured Home Communities and said it is committed to closing on a competing merger deal with Colorado-based ROC Communities Inc.

In August, Manufactured Home, a Chicago-based company led by investor Sam Zell, made an unsolicited cash and stock bid for Chateau, after Chateau had agreed to merge with ROC. It then launched an all-cash tender offer of $26 a share.

Earlier this month, Manufactured Home terminated the tender offer, but made a another bid of $26 in cash per share or operating partnership unit, and added the option of a convertible preferred security for OP unitholders, which was also valued at $26 a share and included long-term tax deferral.
Manufactured Home is considered the largest owner and operator of mobile home parks in the industry, but a Chateau/ROC merger would be bigger.

Chateau rejected the Manufactured Home offers and urged stockholders not to tender shares. Under its revised merger agreement with ROC, each Chateau share would represent 1.0316 shares of the combined company.
"You can lead a horse to water, but you can't force him to drink," Zell said Wednesday at a real estate industry conference in Chicago.
Helfand said the company at this point does not expect to make a further statement.
"If events change in the future, than we would certainly," Helfand told Reuters at the conference. "But for now this is where we stand."
Manufactured Home shares traded unchanged at 19-5/8, and Chateau was off 1/4 at 24-3/8.
